summary_en: The study tests RP2, a genetically modified herpes simplex type 1 virus used as oncolytic immunotherapy, alone or with other cancer drugs, in hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer) and biliary tract cancer. RP2 is injected into the tumor every 2 weeks; in one liver cancer group it is given for 4 doses then every 3 weeks for 4 doses, in another for 8 doses, combined with atezolizumab and bevacizumab, and the liver cancer monotherapy group receives RP2 alone every 2 weeks, while the biliary tract cohort receives durvalumab with RP2 (the biliary schedule is not stated). The record does not state a main outcome measure; it is a Phase 2 study that aims to assess efficacy and safety.
summary_es: El estudio evalúa RP2, un virus del herpes simple tipo 1 modificado genéticamente que se usa como inmunoterapia oncolítica, solo o con otros medicamentos contra el cáncer, en el carcinoma hepatocelular (cáncer de hígado) y en el cáncer de vías biliares. RP2 se inyecta en el tumor cada 2 semanas; en un grupo de cáncer de hígado se da en 4 dosis y luego cada 3 semanas en 4 dosis más, en otro grupo se da en 8 dosis, combinado con atezolizumab y bevacizumab, y el grupo de monoterapia para cáncer de hígado recibe solo RP2 cada 2 semanas, mientras que el grupo de vías biliares recibe durvalumab con RP2 (el esquema para vías biliares no está indicado). El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de Fase 2 que busca evaluar la eficacia y la seguridad.
who_for: Liver cancer: progressed after one prior systemic treatment that included anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy.
Liver cancer: Child-Pugh A liver function.
At least one measurable tumor of 1 cm or more, and injectable tumor(s) totaling at least 1 cm.
Biliary tract cancer: unresectable, not progressed on gemcitabine, platinum chemotherapy and checkpoint inhibitor given for 12 to 24 weeks.
not_for: Liver cancer: Child-Pugh B or C liver function.
Untreated or high-risk esophageal or gastric varices, or significant bleeding in the last 12 months.
Active significant herpes infection, or need for chronic antivirals with anti-herpes activity.
Known brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis.
